summary_paragraph: A man with a history of non-ischemic dilated cardiomyopathy (ejection fraction 20%), COPD, type 2 diabetes, hepatitis C, and crack lung was admitted for acute gastroenteritis following ingestion of undercooked chicken, presenting with nausea, vomiting, diarrhea, and high fever. He developed hypotension and tachycardia, with clinical worsening prompting broad-spectrum antibiotics and fluid resuscitation, which led to transient fluid overload and decompensated heart failure. His course was complicated by acute kidney injury and markedly elevated liver enzymes, both attributed to congestive hepatopathy from impaired cardiac output. Imaging showed stable chronic lung disease with apical infiltrates, treated as community-acquired pneumonia with levofloxacin. He improved with cautious diuresis, returning to his dry weight of 88.4 kg, with normalization of renal and liver function. He was discharged to extended care on his prior heart failure regimen with plans for outpatient follow-up.
